resources.string: A quiet guard for your home network.
DeKoi looks like a storage box on your network. Nothing should ever touch it, so when something does, you will know.
Add a Google account to this phone in its settings, then try again.
Sign-in did not work. Check your connection and try again.
Your DeKoi is watching your network. Nothing has touched it in the last 24 hours.
Something on your network touched your DeKoi in the last 24 hours. Have a look below.
It can’t warn you until it’s back. Check that it has power and that its cable is plugged in.
The first start can take up to 10 minutes. You can leave this screen.
Prepare the memory card with DeKoi Setup on a computer, then scan the code it shows.
Nothing has touched your decoys yet. That is how it should be.

Check that the memory card is in your DeKoi, that it has power, and that the network cable is plugged into your router. If you chose Wi-Fi, check the network name and password. If it still does not appear, prepare the card again with DeKoi Setup.
It will stop sending alerts to this account. To use it again, prepare its memory card with DeKoi Setup.
Someone tried to sign in to the decoy %1$s
Nothing on your network has a reason to sign in to your DeKoi. Someone, or a program, is trying passwords on the devices it finds. That is how break-ins usually start.
Your DeKoi pretends to be a storage box. Ordinary devices leave it alone, so a visit means something on your network is looking around.
A device searched your network for openings
Trying address after address to find open doors is one of the first things an intruder or a harmful program does after getting in.

Look at the details below. If you don’t recognise the device, disconnect it from your network, change your Wi-Fi password, and change the passwords of your important accounts. If it is your own device running network tools, mark it as known.
A device searched your whole network
It asked for the addresses of many devices in a short time. Network tools do this, and so does an intruder mapping what to attack next.
A device is pretending to be another device
It claimed an address that belongs to another device on your network. This is how an attacker puts itself between your devices and the internet to read or change your traffic.
Find the device in the details below. If you don’t recognise it, disconnect it from your network, restart your router and change your Wi-Fi password.
A second device is handing out network settings
Normally only your router gives devices their network settings. Another device doing it can send your traffic through itself.
A second device announces itself as your router
A new device started announcing itself as a router. That can redirect your devices’ traffic through it.
Find the device in the details below. If you don’t recognise it, disconnect it from your network and restart your router.
A device answers questions it should not
Your DeKoi asked for a computer that does not exist, and something answered. Tools that do this trick computers into handing over passwords.
The traffic matched a known pattern of attacks or harmful programs. The details below name the pattern.
While it is offline, your DeKoi can’t warn you. Usually it is a power cut, an unplugged cable or a router restart.
Check that your DeKoi has power and that its network cable is plugged in. It reconnects by itself.
Your DeKoi checks in every minute and is watching your network.
Your DeKoi noticed something it has no plain description for yet.
Hardware address of the real owner
Marked as known. Activity from it no longer counts as a warning.
Devices your DeKoi has seen on your network. New ones are marked.
Phone or tablet with a private address
Your DeKoi lists the devices on your network here within 15 minutes of starting.
On your computer, DeKoi Setup shows a code once the memory card is ready.
The scanner did not work. Type the code shown under the square code in DeKoi Setup instead.
That is not a DeKoi code. Check it and try again.
This code can’t be used. Prepare the card again with DeKoi Setup to get a new one.
Finish setting up your other DeKoi first.
%1$s is linked to your account. Put the card in your DeKoi and plug it in.
When something on your network touches your DeKoi, or your DeKoi goes offline, it can tell you right away. Allow notifications to get these alerts.
This removes your account, your DeKoi devices and all their history. It can’t be undone.
Your DeKoi reports activity on its decoys and the devices it sees on your network. It never collects passwords people type. History is deleted after 90 days.
Can’t reach DeKoi right now. Check your internet connection.
